newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker shareholders endorse merger with RGI.
newsitem.headline: Aker shareholders endorse merger with RGI.

text.p: Aker ASA shareholders on Thursday voted overwhelmingly in favour of merging the Norwegian engineering and offshore group with investment group RGI.
The proposal was adopted by 99.89 percent of A class shares cast and 80.72 percent of A and B class shares together, Aker said following a three-hour extraordinary general meeting.
A two-third majority of shareholders present was sufficient for giving the green light to what has been billed Norway's biggest industrial merger ever.

The merger will bring together one of Norway's oldest companies with a newcomer on the corporate scene. Aker was founded in 1841 while RGI, which has quickly become the world's largest white-fish fishing and processing operation, was listed on the Oslo Bourse only this year.
The combined company, Aker RGI ASA, will have annual revenues of 19 billion crowns and a market capitalisation of nine billion crowns.
The deal had been expected to go through because RGI controls more than 40 percent of Aker voting shares and had won support from most other major shareholders.
The main opponent of the proposed merger, pension fund Folketrygdfondet, said in a statement prior to the meeting it would abstain from voting, removing the last possible hurdle to the fusion.
Folketrygdfondet, which controls about 13 percent of Aker stock, has said it believes the swap rate is disadvantageous for Aker shareholders.
The merger proposal, which values one Aker share at 2.15 RGI shares, was presented by Aker and RGI boards on October 1.

The company will focus on three core areas -- seafood, cement and oil and gas - - but will look for other areas to stretch its newly-found financial muscle, according to Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, Aker chairman and chairman-designated of the new joint board.

Gjelsten is co-owner of RGI with Kjell Inge Roekke, a charismatic entrepreneur who started buying Aker shares aggressively last February and who will have a 33 percent shareholding in the new company.

RGI's other interests include sports goods and outdoor apparel, shipbuilding, real estate, packaging office supplies and finance. Currently registered in the Netherlands Antilles, it will transfer operations to Norway under the merger plan, which is subject to approval by the government.
